description.en-US: The ISO 4217 alphabetic code: VND, USD, EUR. The regex enforces upper case rather than a sanitizer folding it, because the only sanitizers available are none/html/plaintext and a lower-case code should be rejected rather than quietly rewritten. Immutable, because it is what every amount elsewhere in the system is denominated by; changing it would silently reinterpret money already recorded.
The ISO 4217 numeric code, e.g. 704 for VND. Kept as a string because it is an identifier with significant leading zeros, not a quantity.
What is shown next to an amount: ₫, $, €.

Whether the symbol is written before the amount ($15.00) or after it (15.000 ₫). It belongs to the currency rather than to the reader's locale, so an amount reads the same to everyone in the organization.
The name of the major unit, as an amount is spelled out in words: Dollar, Đồng.
The name of the minor unit: Cent, Xu.
The smallest amount this currency is settled in: 1 for VND, 0.01 for USD, 0.05 for a currency settled in nickels. Every amount is rounded to a multiple of it, and decimal_places is derived from it.

How many fractional digits this currency is quoted to: 0 for VND, 2 for USD, 3 for KWD. Maintained by the server from rounding and never written by a client, so the two cannot disagree. This is why money is stored as decimal rather than as an integer count of minor units — the count is a property of the currency, and holding amounts that way would push this number into every caller that reads one.

Whether the acting organization uses this currency: its essential_org_currency row, false without one. Written through this record's create and update, never stored here, so each organization answers for itself.
